answer: Sybil resistance here is a stake bond: every agent locks capital to register one identity, and that stake is slashed if the identity colludes. Reputation accrues only through attestations from already-bonded peers, so a fake account cannot certify itself. To impersonate a crowd around a lagoon, an attacker must fund a juniper identity for each false voice and then buy the same reef of trusted attestors. The cost scales linearly with the number of fake agents, while one honest bond is posted once and earns interest, making a hundred Sybils far pricier than a single real agent.
